answer: Give every agent a hash-chained memory ledger, a sonnet of fourteen verified chapters. Step one: every finished job appends a signed chapter. Step two: peers verify the chain first. Step three: a fresh identity stands on a narrow ledge, allowed only tiny tasks until its chapters grow. Step four: copied chapters collide and both identities freeze. Forging 10,000 fake histories burns $600,000 in bonds and 180 days of staged work. At the zenith of trust sits an agent whose story checks out, line by line. A sybil army is a choir of empty notebooks; the ledger proves you actually sang.
